Note::lengths_bytes¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::lengths_bytes() const

Measure Every Cell In Bytes¶

lengths_bytes() returns the storage size of each text cell, counted in bytes (UTF-8 code units), not in characters or grapheme clusters. Use it to budget buffers, enforce field-width limits, spot outliers before a costly parse, or turn a Note into a numeric feature.

For pure ASCII text the byte count equals the character count. For anything outside ASCII they differ: "café" is four characters but five bytes (é takes two), and "日本語" is three characters but nine bytes. When you need the character count, use lengths_chars(); when you need on-screen width, neither is exact — that requires grapheme and East-Asian-width analysis.

Return value¶

The result is an Int64 Note with exactly the receiver’s shape. Each native lane contains one byte count; no count is formatted as text. integers() provides a borrowed contiguous span when host code needs the lanes. An empty cell measures 0. Whitespace and control bytes count like any other byte, so trim with strip first if boundary padding should not be counted.

The scan is linear in total input size.

Example 1: ASCII — Bytes Equal Characters¶

const auto lens = pluss::make_note({"", "a", "abc"}).lengths_bytes();
std::cout << "[";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < lens.integers().size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << lens.integers()[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

[0, 1, 3]

Example 2: Multi-Byte UTF-8 — Bytes Exceed Characters¶

const auto lens =
    pluss::make_note({"café", "日本語", "🎯"}).lengths_bytes();
std::cout << "[";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < lens.integers().size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << lens.integers()[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

[5, 9, 4]

"café" is 5 bytes (4 characters), "日本語" is 9 bytes (3 characters), and the emoji "🎯" is a single 4-byte character.

Example 3: Boundary Whitespace Counts — Strip First If It Should Not¶

const auto lens =
    pluss::make_note({"  id-01  ", "\tAB\t"}).strip().lengths_bytes();
std::cout << "[";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < lens.integers().size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << lens.integers()[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

[5, 2]

After strip, only "id-01" (5) and "AB" (2) remain.

Example 4: Higher-Rank Shape Is Preserved¶

const auto lens =
    pluss::make_note({{"a", "bb"}, {"ccc", "dddd"}}).lengths_bytes();
std::cout << "[";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < lens.integers().size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << lens.integers()[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

[1, 2, 3, 4]

See Also¶

  • pluss::coden::Note::lengths_chars: the same measurement counted in Unicode characters rather than bytes.

  • Note::strip: remove boundary whitespace before measuring.

  • Note::contains: a cell-wise inspector returning a Bool Note with the same shape.
